To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the georeaction of maize root segments is controlled by endogenous indole-acetic acid (IA A) moving preferentially in an acropetal direction.
the georeaction is a property of intact root apices and is not a consequence of the removal of the root cap.
(a) root growth and geostimulation are regulated by endogenous IAA and ABA and (b) the endogenous IAA/ABA ratio is an important factor in the control of growth and georection of root apices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the control of root elongation and georeaction and with the role of endogenous indolic compounds in this process.
the role of auxins and abscisics in controlling root growth and geostimulation, and the possible interaction between them in this process.
the role of auxins and abscisins in the control of the growth and georeactions of roots.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the control of root apical growth and georeactivity involves a balance of the actions of IAA and ABA, and that the balance is controlled by the endogenous concentrations of the two hormones.
the control of georeaction involves the interaction of endogenous auxin moving acropetally and endogenous inhibitors moving basipetally.
IAA is involved in the normal control of the growth and georeactivity of the root apex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the control of root curvature involves a complex interaction of the effects of endogenous I.AA, exogenous IAA and ABA.

the normal control system of the root growth and geotropism involves a balance between the acropetal transport of endogenous I.A.A. and the basipetal transport of growth inhibitors produced in the root cap cells.

the control of root elongation and georeaction is a dynamic process involving the interaction of endogenous and exogenous IAA and abscisie acid and that the endogenous IAA is not a growth hormone but a growth regulator.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the endogenous auxins in the apical region are involved in the regulation of the georeaction of the maize root.
root georeaction is a highly complex phenomenon, and it may be regulated in different ways in different cultivars of the same species.
the endogenous IAA is not the only factor controlling root growth.
